summary: Two fire towers on Diamond Mountain near Sloatsburg: a 1935 steel tower and a 1966 Aermotor replacement, removed 1986; no source describes the summit site today.

facts.design: Steel tower built in 1935 from the steel of the old Bear Mountain tower; 1966 replacement was an 80-foot Aermotor LS 40 with louvered aluminum windows in the cab
facts.status_note: Both towers removed: the first taken down in 1955, the second removed in 1986.

access.note: A 2020 hiking account describes trails in Harriman State Park that reach the summit. The account does not describe the tower site itself.

visit.trail_note: A yellow-blazed Diamond Mountain Tower Trail and the HTS Trail reach the summit. No source describes any remaining tower structure.

evidence.supports: Location about three miles northeast of Sloatsburg
Listed in Rockland County with status gone
First steel tower built in 1935 by the Palisades State Park Commission from the old Bear Mountain tower steel
evidence.quote: The first steel tower here was constructed using the steel from the old Bear Mt. tower in 1935 by the Palisades State Park Commission.

evidence.supports: First tower taken down in 1955 and its steel stored
evidence.quote: This tower was taken down in 1955, and the steel removed to the Merrit Bank yard for safe keeping.

evidence.supports: 1966 replacement was an 80-foot Aermotor LS 40 with louvered aluminum windows in the cab
evidence.quote: In 1966 the Park Commission purchased and erected an 80' Aermotor LS 40 tower which had louvered aluminum windows in the observation cab.

evidence.supports: Second tower stood twenty years and was removed in 1986
evidence.quote: It stood for twenty years until it too was removed in 1986.

evidence.supports: Park stopped running its fire towers in the early 1980s, citing manpower and budget
evidence.quote: The Park's operation of it's fire towers ceased in the early 1980's because of manpower shortages and budget restrictions.

evidence.supports: DEC deactivated most fire observation stations in 1989
evidence.quote: in 1989, when the Department of Environmental Conservation de-activated most of its fire observation stations.

evidence.supports: The detection system that included the Diamond towers came to a halt in 1989
evidence.quote: The system of fire detection, enhanced by the towers at Fingerboard, Diamond, Jackie Jones and Sterling, came to a halt shortly afterwards

evidence.supports: No photos of either tower have been located
evidence.quote: No photos of either of the Diamond Mt. towers have been located.

evidence.supports: Steel reused at Sterling Fire Tower when Sterling Forest State Park was created in 1998
evidence.quote: Some steel pieces from these towers were used at Sterling Fire Tower to construct handrails and make other repairs when Sterling Forest State Park was created in 1998.

evidence.supports: Summit in Harriman State Park, Rockland County

evidence.quote: Diamond Mountain Tower Trail: Yellow blaze

evidence.supports: Hikers reach the summit on the HTS Trail
evidence.quote: We then took the HTS Trail steeply up the mountain to the top of Diamond Mountain.

notes_for_editor: The tower history rests on a single list entry (Searchable list, Diamond Mt. Fire Tower), with no second source found. The Eastern lookouts Diamond Mountain page gives nothing beyond the county. A search summary attributed the 1935/1955/1966/1986 dates to a hiking blog, but the blog page read does not contain them, so the dates are cited only to the Searchable list. Access rests on one 2020 hiking account. Nothing read says whether any part of the tower remains on the summit.
